page: Vultr vbm-8c-128gb-amd is a bare metal server featuring an AMD EPYC 4345P processor built on the x86_64 architecture. This dedicated hardware configuration delivers 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs running at a base clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The system is equipped with 123.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, providing 7.71 GB of RAM per core. Storage is fully bundled, consisting of a 3890 GB local NVMe SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance type.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU testing, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all placing in the top 10% of tested servers. The passmark memory score also ranks in the top tier. However, multi-core performance metrics, such as stress-ng multi-core and passmark CPU scores, fall into the average range. A notable performance tradeoff is the uncached large-block memory write bandwidth, which is classified in the bottom 25%, contrasting with the average read bandwidths. For lightweight machine learning workloads, the server demonstrates top-tier text generation speeds and strong prompt processing speeds on small 135M models, though performance scales down to average levels on medium 7B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this bare metal server offers high resource density, combining dedicated CPU execution with a substantial allocation of fast DDR5 memory and high-capacity NVMe storage. This makes it highly suitable for workloads requiring dedicated hardware without virtualization overhead. Optimal use cases include database hosting, static web serving, and memory-intensive applications that benefit from high single-core speeds and local NVMe storage, while avoiding workloads heavily dependent on massive multi-threaded parallelization or high-throughput memory writes.
